finding: pd_logistic = 1 / (1 + sas_exp(-predicted_logit)) uses plain polars `/` with a LITERAL numerator. A13 enumerates scalar/literal/aggregate DIVISORS (here the divisor is a column >= 1, so plain `/` is allowed by that list), but the same row also says plain `/` is allowed 'only column by column', which a literal numerator is not. So the rulebook is ambiguous here and the implementer did not flag it (the comment at :207 only asserts it). No output impact: on 2,000,000 random denominators (contiguous and chunked frames) polars `1 / (1 + col)` is bit-identical to numpy IEEE 1.0/(1.0+e) (scratch check_chain.py)
